name: obj_sum
title: Type and size of an object

origin.description: A vector is its type abbreviation, without the shape, followed by its size. Anything vec_is rejects is the type summary alone.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: An object to summarise. Methods are in place for atomic vectors and the usual variants.

origin.details: The result is one string. From pillar 1.6.1 the default method asks vec_ptype_abbr for a vector and type_sum for anything else. Earlier versions always used type_sum. An attribute named short is the compact form. pillar_shaft uses it for a list column when the width is tight. An array stores abbr followed by an opening bracket, the ellipsis, and a closing bracket. A data frame and an atomic vector store the abbreviation alone. Printing this value shows the short attribute when it is set. A function, an environment, and NULL have no short attribute.
origin.value: A single string. Vectors also carry a short attribute.
origin.example:
obj_sum(1:10)
obj_sum(matrix(1:10))
obj_sum(data.frame(a = 1))
obj_sum(Sys.Date())
obj_sum(Sys.time())
obj_sum(mean)

translation.description: The same text. A vector returns a string with a short attribute. A function, Environment, and NULL return a plain string.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A vector, Matrix, DataFrame, Table, List, date, datetime, function, Environment, or NULL. An R list is List([1, 2]). The list [1, 2] is the integer vector 1:2.

translation.details: The abbreviation comes from vec_ptype_abbr with the shape suffix off, then a space, then size_sum. A Matrix or a Table, and any other value with a dim that is not a DataFrame, stores short as abbr, an opening bracket, symbol["ellipsis"], and a closing bracket. Otherwise short is the abbreviation. cli.unicode TRUE uses … and FALSE uses .... The example prints the text and then the short attribute. mean is fn and has no short attribute.
translation.value: A string. Vectors are a str subclass with a short attribute.
translation.example:
from datetime import date, datetime

from cli._options import options as cli_options

cli_options(**{"cli.unicode": True})

from pillar._vec import DataFrame, Matrix
from pillar.summary import obj_sum


def mean(values):
    return values


def show(value):
    print(value)
    short = getattr(value, "short", None)
    print("short:", "absent" if short is None else short)


show(obj_sum(list(range(1, 11))))
show(obj_sum(Matrix(list(range(1, 11)), 10)))
show(obj_sum(DataFrame({"a": [1]})))
show(obj_sum(date.today()))
show(obj_sum(datetime.now()))
show(obj_sum(mean))
